newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - April 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - April 7.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY

- The National Union of Metalworkers of South Africa (NUMSA) and the National Union of Mineworkers (NUM) are to declare a dispute with Eskom over the government's plan for privatisation in the electricity supply sector.

- Corporates and individuals could soon pay local tax on all their passive or investment income, regardless of the source, and passive income could be taxed on a worldwide basis, according to recommendations by the Katz commission on tax.
- South African Airways will show an unaudited loss of 345 million rand for the year ending March 1997, but has tabled a budget which will allow it to break even during this financial year.

- National police commissioner George Fivaz denied he had threatened to resign, but indicated that a widening chasm between the police department and the ministry was serious enough to require presidential mediation.
BUSINESS REPORT
- The municipal workers' union, SAMWU, has declared war on privatisation and will hold pickets across the country to protest against the effective privatisation of some water supply services.
- SAA's top management structure would be radically restructured in the near future, according to Zukile Nomvete, the Transnet executive director responsible for SAA.

- Xisaka Investment and Trading, whose shareholders include the South African Railway and Harbours Workers' Union, said it was negotiating with a leading European company to establish a refinery to beneficiate nonferrous scrap metals and other hazardous waste material covered by the U.N.'s Basel Convention.

- Agriculture Minister Derek Hanekom urged the high court to postpone for four months considering KWV's application to convert to a company. This would allow time to consider the full implications of the proposed conversion and devise an alternative statutory system for the wine industry.
- Sharp increases in the price of quality South African wine have paved the way for a significant increase in wine imports aimed at the middle and upper end of the local market.
SAKE-BEELD

- The National Union of Metalworkers is demanding wage increases of 12 percent above inflation for lower-level workers in the engineering sector and 16 percent above inflation for motor industry workers. Consumer inflation is currently running at 9.8 percent annually.

- The Katz commission on South African taxation wants the current system to remain for active income, but to widen the net to allow local tax to be levied on passive or investment income anywhere in the world.
- Coca-Cola is apparently considering plans to amalgamate its bottlers and distributors in southern Africa into a stronger regional company.
- Informal "spaza" shops have been mushrooming in black townships in the Western Cape, and their turnover is estimated to have reached around two billion rand per year.
- Sentrachem is expected to show a loss for the six months to end-February, after the write-off of 281 million rand in its Sanachem subsidiary, analysts said.
THE STAR
- South African sports fans, accustomed to victory celebrations since the country's readmission into the international sports arena, endured humiliation on all fronts at the weekend.

- Tongues are already wagging within the ANC and its structures following the surprise nomination by the ANC Youth League of Mpumalanga Premier Mathews Phosa for the deputy presidency of the organisation.
- Zairean peace talks hosted by South Africa appeared to be making progress, according to diplomatic sources.
